learningObjective: Interpret an Inductor scheduler log showing that a chain broke into multiple kernels at a reduction boundary.

canonicalClaims.claim: TorchInductor's scheduler keeps producer and consumer as separate kernels when their iteration spaces are incompatible; a reduction that produces a shape-`[N,1]` output followed by a pointwise chain over the original `[N,D]` shape often does not fuse into a single kernel in default configurations.
conditions: The user has not applied a specialized fusion configuration.
nonImplications: Does not imply Inductor never fuses reduction with pointwise; the softmax pattern fuses.
Does not imply the split kernels perform poorly; each may still be highly optimized.

misconceptions.claim: Inductor never fuses reductions with pointwise ops.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Softmax epilogue and many similar patterns fuse.

misconceptions.claim: Two Inductor kernels always indicate a graph break.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Multiple kernels can come from scheduler decisions inside one Inductor graph.

misconceptions.claim: Inductor emits one kernel per Python op regardless of dependence.
The reduction runs on CPU when the pointwise runs on GPU.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both kernels target CUDA for CUDA inputs.

implementationFacts: Scheduler decisions can be dumped via `TORCH_LOGS=inductor`
Fusion across an iteration-space mismatch typically requires the reduction result to broadcast, which may not fit the scheduler's chosen tiling
performanceScenarios: Two-kernel structures pay one extra HBM round-trip for the reduction output; whether this matters depends on `N`.
